steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (180 degrees C).
Mix oil and 1 cup sugar in a large bowl. Add egg; beat well.
Stir in molasses, 2 cups flour, baking soda, cinnamon, ginger, and cloves. Add more flour to make a firm dough if needed.
Shape dough into 1 1/4-inch balls. Roll in 1/3 cup sugar. Place 3 inches apart on an ungreased baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until tops crack, 12 to 14 minutes. Remove cookies from the baking sheet and cool on a rack.

raw_recipe.headline: Crackle Top Molasses Cookies
raw_recipe.description: The molasses crackle cookies from this recipe taste like gingersnaps, thanks to ginger, cinnamon, and cloves.

review.reviewBody:
These were SO GOOD! I followed some other suggestions and here's what I ended up using: 2/3 cup canola oil; 1/2 cup white sugar; 1/2 cup brown sugar; 1 egg; 1/4 cup molasses; 1 cup all-purpose flour; 1 cup whole wheat flour; 2 t. baking soda; 1/4 t. salt; 1 t. ground cinnamon; 1 heaping t. ground ginger; 1 t. vanilla; 1/2 heaping t. ground cloves; 1/3 cup sugar (for rolling dough balls).

I baked them for 10 minutes. They turned out perfectly. This is definitely going in my recipe box!!!

Everything you always wanted in a molasses cookie: chewy crackled outsides, soft cakey insides, with a wonderful fragrance that makes the whole house smell like Christmas. I love that these cookies use no butter and could easily be made for vegan friends. I used olive oil and palm sugar for a very healthy version, and they came out just as good as with regular sugar. I added extra spices since I like mine spicy - 2 teaspoons cinammon, 1.5 teaspoons ginger, heaping 1/2 teaspoon of cloves. I flattened mine slightly as the first batch did not spread, probably my oven's fault. I also dipped the tops on sparkling sugar instead of the regular kind. My new go-to molasses cookie.

My husband loves these cookies. I made two batches, one mixed by hand, and the other with an electric mixer. If you want a more traditional flat cookie, use the electric mixer. Otherwise, mix by hand for a thicker cookie. I also used the advise from other reviews and used 1/2 cup brown sugar and white sugar. I didn't have any cloves at home, so I used 1tsp. ground nutmeg instead, and they were still spicy and delicious. I also only baked them for about 10 minutes, and they were perfect.

I had a hard time getting this right due to high altitude and bad planning. But even the bad batches got devoured. On my third attempt I reduced the flour to about 1.5C, reduced the oven temperature to 325F, and increased bake time by 10min. I live in a very arid climate and at about 6500ft.

I am putting this in my recipe file... What I really liked about it is the oil instead of butter. Sometimes it's good to have recipes with other options. I did go with 3/4 cup white sugar and 1/4 cup brown sugar.... And added 1/4 tsp of nutmeg. I also skipped rolling them in the sugar.
 I baked them for 10 minutes 
Easy, delicious and the perfect "after" the holiday rich goodies. I like them especially with tea. I will definitely be making these again. My hubby really liked them too.

Make sure the dough is really thick or it will be too sticky to roll - I used about 2 1/4 cups of flour. I also used half brown half white sugar, but next time might use 3/4 if not even all brown (but white for rolling). 
I baked them 7-8 min, but I also made smaller cookies- the dough balls expand a LOT! About double the amount choc chip cookies expand, so if you want normal size cookies use less than a teaspoon (cutlery-size spoon, not the measurement).
The wax paper trick works, thanks for sharing! Cookies are still soft after letting them cool on wax paper instead of cooling racks.
Bottom line: definitely a keeper! Edit: a year later, still loving these cookies!

WOW! These are REALLY good! I've made two batches. The first I made almost exactly as directed, except I used Canola oil and used 3/4 c sugar and 1/4 cup brown sugar. The second batch, I used butter flavored crisco instead of canola oil. I have made the first batch and they are amazing! I pulled the first tray out at 8 minutes, but the second tray needed 11 to start getting crackly. I also baked them on parchment paper so that I could move them directly to my cooling table, instead of cooling them on wax paper as I read. Will post more on how that works later! I believe I will be making a couple more batches of this cookie for the holiday season. They will go fast!
Beautiful and delicious! I tossed in a little nutmeg too! Refrigerate the dough for about an hour before making the cookies. This makes it a lot easier to work with.

I ran out of olive oil so used butter instead. After softening it in the microwave, the butter worked in well with the batter. No need for a mixer-master. No extra flour needed. I rolled in plastic wrap and cooled for about an hour, so the dough was easy to slice and roll. I did not roll in sugar. I made smaller balls so I can fit 12 at a time in my toaster oven tray. Made two batches in less than 40 minutes. Super crispy/crunchy and just the right size for snacking or dredging in vanilla ice cream! BTW, the whole house smelled wonderful--better than using a scented candle!

Yummy cookies! Very easy, not at all too spicy. Perfect. I did change just a few things after reading the reviews. I used 1c white flour, 1c whole wheat flour, 1/2c brown sugar and 1/2c white sugar. I baked them for 8 minutes and they were done. I did let them cool longer than I usually do right on the cookie sheet. They are soft, but hold their shape nicely. Personally, I prefer my cookies to have more crunch. Next time, they'll go right on the cooling rack. I made them last night, and I think they're ALL gone :-)

This is an excellent recipe! My first time making molasses cookies and it was so simple. I followed a few suggestions of other reviewers. I did 3/4 cup white sugar and 1/4 cup brown sugar, I cut the ginger in half, and added a 1/2 tsp of vanilla and salt. Also if you want a chewy cookie only bake 7-8 minutes. So easy and super delicious!
Gads! this brings back memories. I split the white sugar and added brown by 1/2 cup each...these are favourites!
The cookies are just the right size and the recipe was simple and user-friendly. Easy enough to make with the grandkids.
Very easy and quick to make. Made recipe as written. Got rave reviews from family and friends.

What a great way to utilize molasses ! This is a great recipe for a fall season cookie that’s going to be a crowd-pleaser. The ratios were spot on and the cookies came out perfect. They have such a fun texture, not dry at all. The flavor also was well balanced, not too sweet at all, with an elegant gingery bite. This will pair so well with a light tea or coffee.

These are like little ginger-molasses pillows when warm, and chewy when room temp. I typically use another recipe but this will be my new "go to" for the perfect crackle look on top! Next time, I'll add a little salt to the recipe for personal preference, but it's perfect as is!
I've made these many times with only one modification - roll them in turbinado instead of white sugar. It puts them over the top!
V. Good
Delicious... To cut down on cholesterol I use canola oil..
I made these for Christmas and only got to eat one. Our kids and grandkids took them all home with them. This year I'll make more only I'll hide some for myself before they get here.
